hypothesis_text: Statistical deviations in perpetual futures basis relative to spot prices (basis_reversion = -zscore((futures - spot)/spot, 8h)) on midcap altcoins (BNBUSDT, SOLUSDT, XRPUSDT) reflect temporary liquidity and inventory imbalances among market makers rather than permanent fundamental price discovery. Over 1h to 4h horizons, basis dislocations mean-revert towards spot parity, producing positive price returns when basis is depressed (discounted futures) and negative returns when basis is elevated (rich futures), especially when conditioned on order book depth imbalance and extreme leverage positioning.
narrative: Perpetual futures prices frequently diverge from underlying spot prices due to sudden retail flow surges, liquidation bursts, or speculative position building. Market makers absorb this one-sided inventory but face capital and risk limits, causing basis spreads to stretch beyond 1.5 standard deviations over 8-hour rolling windows. Because perpetual contracts feature continuous funding mechanisms and spot arbitrageurs enforce parity over multi-hour horizons, these basis dislocations are transient. Once aggressive order flow subsides, market makers re-quote towards spot parity and spot-futures arbitrageurs close the gap, driving predictable price recovery in the direction of spot parity over 1h to 4h. Conditioning on order book depth asymmetry (depth_imbalance_10 tail gate) isolates periods where resting book absorption is strained, while open interest (oi_zscore_24h tail gate) identifies stretched leverage regimes where unwinding accelerates reversion.
research_rationale: The anchor signal XL_BNBUSDT_f22785898fff captures the symmetric extreme tails of 8h basis dislocation (|basis_reversion| > 1.5) on BNBUSDT at 15m cadence with 14.6% event density (18,802 matched rows, 430 independent active days across midcap altcoins), showing 0.0018 autocorrelation at 1d and balanced positive/negative split (9,617 vs 9,185 bars). In the alpha cemetery for basis_reversion (2,822 trials, 194 T1 survivors), the dominant failure modes are T0.04-IC-STAT (1,725 kills) and T1.10-ICIR (428 kills), indicating that unconstrained continuous trading suffers from noise and insufficient signal-to-noise ratio. Our design directly addresses this by gating on orderbook depth imbalance (depth_imbalance_10 gate_tail, 280 projected T1 days) and open interest leverage extremes (oi_zscore_24h gate_tail, 279 projected T1 days), which prune low-conviction noise bars and concentrate on high-impact liquidity dislocations. The spread coupling with taker_buy_ratio_1h follows prior empirical evidence in midcap altcoins where basis_reversion x taker_buy_ratio achieved a 23.5% T1 survival rate (17 trials, 4 survivors). Search scope 'full' is chosen to explore both the explicit authored gate combinations and the automated mutator grid over these three validated economic roles.
